title: review
description: Stage output contract: the PR was reviewed against the task goal and code quality.

tests_meaningful.description: independent test-validate verdict (#13/#541): do the change's tests meaningfully exercise it (would they fail if it regressed)? An explicit false rejects the review even when approved. REVIEW is the only stage that judges this. true needs a mutation_checks entry that failed a test, or a tests_not_checked_reason. null means no verdict: only for a change with genuinely no test surface or a check nothing could settle, with tests_not_checked_reason saying why. An approval with neither proof nor reason is sent back by the engine; one with a reason passes and is evented (test_validation_skipped), never recorded as proven

mutation_checks.description: #541: the mutations this review applied to prove tests_meaningful (empty when none was run). A structured record, so a missing check is visible rather than hidden behind a pass

failed_tests.description: ids of the tests that failed on this mutation; empty means it survived

blocking.description: #614: whether this SURVIVED mutation (empty failed_tests) opens a fix cycle. The engine, not the reviewer, acts on it: true only when the mutation sits on behaviour the task spec requires or on a guard the project marks money-path/safety, and it needs a non-blank blocking_reason naming which, or the engine demotes it (evented). Every other survivor is reported once as a noted gap in non_blocking, never as a blocking issue. Defaults to false. Ignored on a mutation that failed a test

blocking_reason.description: #614: required when blocking is true: the spec requirement or money-path/safety guard this survivor falls on. A blocking survivor with no reason is demoted to a noted gap

tests_not_checked_reason.description: #541: why no mutation settled tests_meaningful (no behavioral test surface, an inconclusive workspace, a lane with no disposable workspace). Accepted in place of proof and evented as unproven

workspace_origin.description: #411: where the TEST RUNNER in this review workspace resolved the code it imported. Asked for only when the workspace's toolchain origin could not be verified structurally (the project declares no #391 origin hooks) — a review workspace provisioned by copy can import a SIBLING worktree's source, which fabricates a survived mutation and a spurious failure alike. `confirmed`: a collected test printed an exercised module's `__file__` and it lies under this workspace. `mismatched`: it resolved outside this workspace, so command results here are about another checkout's code. `not_checked`: the check was not run. An absent value is recorded as `not_checked` and evented (review_workspace_origin_unconfirmed) — never as `confirmed`. Report-only: it does not gate approval, because a reviewer who ran nothing dynamic can still review a diff correctly

severity.description: suggestion-only rejections auto-approve (the severity gate); critical/important drive the fix cycle

issues.description: blocking issues (empty when approved). Prefer the structured object form — severity gates disposition, file/line/suggested_fix make the fix cycle actionable

non_blocking.description: findings that do NOT block approval; each may carry a `disposition` that gates what the engine does with it at finalize. An explicit `file`, chosen deliberately with justification, becomes a follow-up issue (up to a small per-task cap). An explicit `fixup` is APPLIED in this PR — the engine re-opens IMPLEMENT→…→REVIEW once for the whole batch of them. An absent disposition and `fix_now`/`drop` findings are surfaced in the completion note ('Noted, not filed') but never filed and never applied, so nothing is silently dropped (empty if none)

disposition.description: filing threshold. Choose `file` deliberately, with justification, only when a maintainer would put this on the backlog independently — out-of-scope (different subsystem / needs its own design) OR non-trivial (real work/risk). NEVER `file` these — they are `drop` (or `fixup` if trivial-in-blast-radius): cosmetic consistency ('move X to match Y', rename for symmetry), speculative tunability (expose N knobs nobody asked for), premature instrumentation (dashboards/metrics for a feature not yet exercised), redundant convenience (a wrapper for already-exposed capability). `fixup`: a trivial nit WITHIN the blast radius of this change (a docstring the edit made stale, a guard/type on a touched line) — not worth a ticket, so the engine APPLIES it in place via one bounded re-implement cycle rather than filing it. `fix_now`: noted in the completion note only — the engine does NOT apply it; prefer `fixup` when you want the nit actually fixed. `drop`: a real-but-untracked observation, noted and moved on. An absent disposition is noted, not filed; filing requires explicit `file`.

improvement.description: self-improvement loop: the single highest-value forward-looking improvement this task suggests for the PROJECT/roadmap (not a fix for this PR). Emit one ONLY if a maintainer would independently prioritize it — a concrete trigger or demonstrated need, not a nice-to-have. Do NOT emit: speculative tunability (expose N knobs nobody asked for), premature instrumentation (dashboards for a feature not yet exercised), or convenience wrappers for already-exposed capability. Omit if none clears the bar (it is optional). The engine files an improvement as an enhancement issue at finalize only when it carries an explicit `file` disposition, chosen deliberately with justification.

disposition.description: same filing threshold as a non_blocking finding. Choose `file` deliberately, with justification, to file an enhancement issue. `fixup`: apply as a trivial in-place change in THIS PR — do not file. `fix_now`/`drop`: surfaced in the completion note, neither filed nor applied. An absent disposition is noted, not filed; filing requires explicit `file`.

retrospective.description: self-improvement loop: one lesson this task teaches about the ORCHESTRATION PROCESS (prompts/stages/tooling/lanes), not the code. Rendered in the completion note. Omit if none.

detail.description: what we learned / what to change

target.description: optional concrete harness artifact this lesson concerns
